samples.scenario: Customer support agent responding to a legitimate customer inquiry about accessing files in a shared cloud storage folder

technical_data.email_body: Dear Customer, you can access your shared files via the secure link provided. Please ensure you are logged in with your authenticated account. Let us know if you need further assistance.

indicators: Communication sent from verified corporate email address
Support ticket exists and matches the inquiry
Agent authenticated through corporate SSO prior to responding
Email uses encrypted SMTP channel
Content aligns with typical support guidance
samples.activity_type: Authentic business communication - Customer support interaction
samples.business_justification: Responding to customer queries about file access is a routine and necessary part of customer service operations.

samples.scenario: Google Cloud Storage bucket configured with uniform bucket-level access disabled and IAM policy granting allUsers the role roles/storage.objectViewer, exposing confidential project data publicly.
indicators: IAM policy binding includes allUsers with roles/storage.objectViewer
Audit logs showing anonymous storage.objects.get requests from external IPs
Access logs showing HTTP 200 GET requests for sensitive objects without authentication
Unusual user agents such as wget in access logs accessing confidential files
samples.detection_method: Enable and monitor GCP Cloud Asset Inventory and IAM policy analyzer to detect public access bindings. Review Cloud Audit Logs for anonymous read operations on storage buckets. Aggregate GCS access logs and alert on high volume or unusual anonymous GET requests. Use anomaly detection on user agents and source IP addresses.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1078 - Valid Accounts (anonymous access via misconfiguration)
T1567 - Exfiltration Over Web Service

samples.scenario: Google Cloud Storage bucket configured with uniform bucket-level access disabled and IAM policy granting allUsers read and write permissions, exposing customer PII data to public with potential modification.
indicators: IAM policy binding includes allUsers with roles/storage.objectViewer and roles/storage.objectCreator
Cloud Audit Logs showing storage.objects.get requests from unknown IPs with anonymous user agent
Access logs showing successful HTTP 200 GET requests to sensitive objects without authentication
Use of common command line tools such as wget for downloading objects publicly
samples.detection_method: Enable uniform bucket-level access on GCS buckets to enforce IAM policies at bucket level. Deploy GCP Security Command Center and monitor audit logs for anonymous access patterns. Analyze storage access logs for high volume or unusual read/write from public IPs. Alert on IAM policy changes that grant public access.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1078 - Valid Accounts (anonymous public access)
T1567 - Exfiltration Over Web Service

samples.scenario: Google Cloud Storage bucket with uniform bucket-level access disabled and legacy ACLs granting allAuthenticatedUsers write access, allowing authenticated but unauthorized users to upload malicious files.
indicators: Legacy ACLs granting allAuthenticatedUsers WRITER access
Cloud Audit Logs showing storage.objects.insert performed by external authenticated users
Access logs showing uploads from unexpected principals with gsutil user agent
Presence of suspicious executable files uploaded to bucket
samples.detection_method: Enable uniform bucket-level access to disable legacy ACLs. Audit bucket ACLs for allAuthenticatedUsers write permissions. Monitor Cloud Audit Logs for unexpected object insertions by external identities. Use malware scanning on uploaded files to detect malicious payloads.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1078 - Valid Accounts (authenticated users via ACL misconfiguration)
T1204 - User Execution (uploading malware)
T1567 - Exfiltration Over Web Service

Successful status code (200)

samples.scenario: Azure Blob Storage container mistakenly set to 'Container' public access level, allowing anonymous users to enumerate and download confidential HR records.

technical_data.HTTP_GET_request_captured_in_Azure_Front:
GET /confidential-records/employee_salaries.xlsx HTTP/1.1
Host: hrstorage.blob.core.windows.net
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7)
Accept: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet

indicators: Blob container ACL set to 'Container' allowing anonymous list and read
Activity logs showing anonymous 'List Blobs' operations
Storage analytics logs with successful anonymous GetBlob requests
Increased anonymous traffic to sensitive container paths
samples.detection_method: Use Azure Security Center to identify containers with public access enabled. Enable Azure Storage analytics and monitor for anonymous read/list operations. Configure alerts for changes to blob container publicAccess property. Restrict container access to authorized identities only.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1078 - Valid Accounts (anonymous access via misconfiguration)
T1567 - Exfiltration Over Web Service

samples.scenario: Daily automated backup of S3 bucket data to a secure archival storage
indicators: Operations performed by a known backup service role
API calls conform to expected backup sequence (ListObjects, GetObject, PutObject)
Consistent timing of activity (daily at 2 AM UTC)
Successful API status codes (200)
Data transferred matches typical backup volume (~100MB)
samples.business_justification: Regular backups are essential for data durability and disaster recovery compliance.

samples.scenario: IT administrator updating user account permissions in the cloud IAM system following a routine quarterly review

samples.scenario: Security monitoring service polling S3 bucket access logs for anomaly detection

Reads performed regularly every hour

No errors or abnormal status codes

samples.scenario: AWS S3 bucket configured with a bucket policy allowing public list (s3:ListBucket) and read (s3:GetObject) access, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of marketing materials and internal presentations.
indicators: Bucket policy allowing s3:ListBucket and s3:GetObject to Principal '*'
CloudTrail logs showing anonymous ListBucket requests from unusual IP addresses
S3 access logs with multiple HTTP 200 GET requests for sensitive files
Unusual user agents such as python-requests used in access logs
samples.detection_method: Implement least privilege bucket policies, remove public list permissions. Use AWS Config rules to detect publicly listable buckets. Monitor CloudTrail for anonymous ListBucket or GetObject calls. Analyze S3 access logs for bulk downloads or repeated anonymous requests.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1078 - Valid Accounts (anonymous access)
T1567 - Exfiltration Over Web Service

samples.scenario: AWS S3 bucket configured with a bucket ACL granting 'Everyone' READ and WRITE permissions, allowing attackers to list, read, and overwrite backup files containing customer credentials.
indicators: Bucket ACL grants READ and WRITE permissions to AllUsers group
CloudTrail logs showing anonymous PutObject calls indicating public write access
S3 access logs confirming successful PUT requests from unknown IPs
Use of AWS CLI with anonymous credentials to modify objects
samples.detection_method: Audit S3 bucket ACLs to remove public WRITE permissions. Use AWS Config managed rules to detect public bucket ACLs. Monitor CloudTrail for anonymous PutObject or DeleteObject events. Alert on unexpected modifications to backup files in sensitive buckets.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1078 - Valid Accounts (anonymous via ACL misconfiguration)
T1567 - Exfiltration Over Web Service
T1570 - Lateral Tool Transfer (usage of AWS CLI to manipulate objects)

samples.scenario: Daily automated backup of critical corporate documents from AWS S3 bucket to a secure archive storage
indicators: Requests originate from known backup automation role
API calls follow expected backup schedule (daily at 02:00 UTC)
All requests authenticated using valid IAM role with least privilege
No anomalous IP addresses or unusual data volumes
No failed authentication or access denied errors
samples.business_justification: Daily backups are required to ensure data durability and disaster recovery compliance for critical business documents.
